bull_case: Daily global data can become a default sensing layer for defense, agriculture, insurance, infrastructure and AI agents.
bear_case: Free public imagery, higher-resolution competitors and lower-cost constellations can commoditize raw pixels faster than Planet monetizes analytics.
thesis: Planet is changing Earth observation from scarce, task-driven imagery into high-cadence data infrastructure. The key innovation is not only satellite hardware but the accumulated daily archive, automated delivery and AI-query layer.

evidence.claim: Q2 revenue grew 58% y/y and recurring ACV was 98%.
NGA, Germany, European defense and Rwanda contracts broaden adoption beyond one vertical.

counterevidence: Satellite services can raise revenue growth while also increasing hardware, launch and execution intensity versus pure imagery subscriptions.
unknowns: Normalized satellite-services gross margin, long-run owner FCF/share, and customer concentration after current sovereign contract ramp.
falsifiers: If NDR falls below 100%, RPO/backlog contract materially, or owner FCF/share turns persistently negative despite revenue growth, the thesis is downgraded.
next_checks: Next 10-Q: revenue mix, RPO/backlog, NDR, adjusted FCF, SBC, ATM issuance and capex

subscores.rationale: Daily global revisit plus cloud distribution turns geospatial monitoring from episodic tasking into continuous data infrastructure.
Revenue +58%, 98% recurring ACV, NDR 109%, and sovereign contracts show scaled adoption.
Imagery, AI analytics, dedicated capacity and sovereign satellite services create multiple adjacent value pools.

uncertainties.rationale: Rapid business-model mix shift and early profitability make long-run normalization uncertain.
